objective: Review commit b7bc4f2 (fff follows directory links by default) for correctness and regressions.
scope: Worktree /home/user/holyagent-0.3.2-fff, branch release/0.3.2/feat/fff-follow-links; review `git diff becf69e b7bc4f2`. Requirement: setup no longer writes followSymlinks: false to pi-fff.json so fff follows directory links by its own default; every other fff override is unchanged; a followSymlinks: false is removed only when the setup record names it as HolyAgent-written and it still equals false, never a value set by hand; docs/pi/search.md states the new default and its consequence.
Check the revert path when the capability is turned off, the record handling, and that tests fail without the change.
constraints: Work only inside /home/user/holyagent-0.3.2-fff; never check out a branch, commit or make any git write in /home/user/holyagent or any other worktree, and make no edits.
Never start pi or make live Kimi, Codex or OpenAI requests; unit tests only.
Report blocking findings with file:line and a concrete failure scenario; report in under 400 words.

criteria.text: The change meets the requirement without regressions in setup, revert or record handling
Tests cover the new default and the cleanup and would fail without the change

result:
result: no blockers. The change meets the requirement and the new tests would fail on the base.

Built-in `/code-review` ran on `becf69e...b7bc4f2` through the Skill tool, and the loaded text was the built-in. It returned 5 findings; each is classified below.

checks-run:
- `bun test` on setup-pi-settings, setup-capabilities and pi/tools tests -> exit 0, 171 pass, 0 fail.
- `bunx --no-install mise run verify` in `/home/user/holyagent-0.3.2-fff` -> exit 0 (type-check and lint clean, 3401 tests pass, 0 fail). I read the output tail; I did not confirm the format check line.
- I did not run the tests against the base. "Fails without the change" is from reading the diff.
- Never run, only read: a live `pi` session with fff.

findings (blockers: none):
- Built-in 1, `src/pi/fff/settings.ts:21`, symlink exposure: rejected as a blocker. Following links by default is the stated requirement, and both the doc and the settings comment name the consequence and the opt-out. Optional: the maintainer owns that trade-off.
- Built-in 2, `setup/pi-settings.ts:347`, removal on upgrade without consent: rejected. The requirement asks for exactly this. The record names the key and its value, so a hand-set `false` is never removed. At project scope `locate` skips the file. In both the `pi.enable`-off path and the capability-off path the same `revertFile` removes it only when the record names it and it still equals `false`.
- Built-in 3, `REVERTABLE` bolt-on: optional. It works. The retired leaf is never in a plan, so it is cleared while the capability is on, and the record is forgotten (tested). A `retiredSettings` field on the patch would tie it to `capabilities.ts`.
- Built-in 4, missing tests: optional.
  - Covered: new default written (`setup-pi-settings.test.ts` "never writes followSymlinks"); recorded `false` removed with the record forgotten; unrecorded `false` kept.
  - Not covered: the retired key under capability-off, `pi.enable` off and `--dry-run`. These share the generic `revertFile` path, which is tested for `mode`, so the risk is low.
  - Not covered: the case where the user changes the value to `true` after setup. That path (`kept followSymlinks true (setup wrote false)`) is no longer tested for `followSymlinks`.
- Built-in 5, `docs/pi/search.md:9`, "setup keeps it": optional. It is accurate for a hand-set `false`, and the same paragraph says the next setup removes the 0.3.1-recorded `false`. A one-clause note that you re-add `false` after the upgrade run would remove the ambiguity.

Own review: other source and test edits are consistent. The tests drop `followSymlinks` from the expected `pi-fff.json`, the added and removed report lines, and the doctor "lacking" line. Generated dist files were rebuilt in the same commit. No leftover `followSymlinks` references in source.

evidence:
The change meets the requirement without regressions in setup, revert or record handling: `FFF_OVERRIDE_SETTINGS` is `{mode:"override"}` (`src/pi/fff/settings.ts`). `REVERTABLE` adds `FFF_RETIRED_SETTINGS`, and `revertFile` filters by record name and value. The docs state the default and its consequence (`docs/pi/search.md`). `mise run verify` exits 0.
Tests cover the new default and the cleanup and would fail without the change: `setup-pi-settings.test.ts` has three new tests (never writes it; removes the recorded `false` with the record forgotten; keeps an unrecorded `false`). The `PI_FFF`, `setup-capabilities` and `tools.test.ts` expectations drop the key, so the base's `followSymlinks: false` write would fail them.
checks-run: the `bun test` and `mise run verify` runs above, both exit 0.
findings: no blockers; four optional notes (REVERTABLE design, retired-key test gaps, doc clause, symlink trade-off).
